when generating the `hashCode` of an element, we do use the size returned by `__iterate`. But in case of `Ordered` element, the internal representation of the underlying list might contain undefined elements :

Example:

const m \= OrderedMap({a:'a', b:'b'}).remove('a')

m.size is 1, the `__iterate` function will iterate only one time on the `b` key, but the internal `_list` element, will have two elements: `[undefined, ['b', 'b']]`:

[![image](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/1398469/350908574-ec4736a0-fbfd-4ae0-b860-6eccbb1e54a5.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..-JbAyutOY5o7XGLgWJBM9nCJ7UPeZ9cXaA8kEXkUEkg)](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/1398469/350908574-ec4736a0-fbfd-4ae0-b860-6eccbb1e54a5.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..-JbAyutOY5o7XGLgWJBM9nCJ7UPeZ9cXaA8kEXkUEkg)  
See [https://runkit.com/jdeniau/immutable-hashcode-using-internal-list-size](https://runkit.com/jdeniau/immutable-hashcode-using-internal-list-size)

I think that we should not use the value returned by `__iterate`, and use the object size directly.

Fixes [#2002](https://github.com/immutable-js/immutable-js/issues/2002)

part.text: The bug: `__iterate`'s return value for ordered collections can exceed the real size (internal list holes after removals), and since `hashCode` is cached in `__hash`, `deepEqual` also fails when hashes are precomputed. Let me confirm in OrderedMap, then apply the fix in this repo's `hashCollection` (which lives in `src/Range.js`).

Confirmed the root cause: `OrderedMap.__iterate` (src/OrderedMap.js:64) delegates to the internal `_list`, whose returned iteration count includes holes left by removed entries, so `hashCollection` computed hashes from an inflated size. Applying the fix in this repo's `hashCollection`:

part.text:
Fixed. The root cause: for ordered collections, `hashCollection` (src/Range.js:205) used the value returned by `__iterate` as the size for `murmurHashOfSize`, but `OrderedMap.__iterate` delegates to the internal `_list` whose count includes holes left by removed entries — so `OrderedSet`/`OrderedMap` with identical elements got different `hashCode()` values depending on construction history (and equality failed too, since `deepEqual` short-circuits on mismatched cached `__hash`).

The fix uses `collection.size` instead, matching the upstream resolution. All 44 test suites (685 tests) pass.
